name: enigma
desc: Puzzle game inspired by Oxyd and Rock'n'Roll
why: A puzzle game in the Oxyd tradition is a rare, excellent old-school title, though it is a graphical game rather than a terminal one.

brief.what_it_is: Enigma is a free, graphical puzzle game, not a terminal tool. You control a small black marble with the mouse and must find and uncover all pairs of identical Oxyd stones in each landscape. The game is built on the Oxyd tradition, with hidden traps, mazes, laser beams and many puzzles standing between the marble and the stones. It ships with more than 1000 main-pack levels plus tutorials and other level sets. It runs on Windows, Mac OS X and most Linux and Unix systems.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a tribute: it is 'inspired by Oxyd on the Atari ST and Rock'n'Roll on the Amiga.' The developers are a small volunteer group who keep it going and invite contributions of code, levels, translations and graphics.

commands_seen.context: Build and install from source in the enigma directory on a Unix machine, per the README's Compiling Enigma section. The README says to install the libraries listed in doc/REQUIREMENTS first.

brief.install_notes: Windows and Mac OS X: download the .exe or .dmg from the homepage and double-click to start. Linux and other Unix: the homepage says binaries may or may not exist for your distribution and may or may not work, and points to a Linux howto and a download page. The README's own advice is to compile from source, which needs the libraries listed in doc/REQUIREMENTS. Windows and Mac builds have separate docs at doc/README.mingw32 and doc/README.macosx. The 1.30 news item says the move from SDL 1.2 to SDL 2.0 is done, which suggests SDL2 is a build dependency. The brew entry's executable name is 'enigma'. No accounts or hardware are needed.
brief.standout: It is a faithful, long-running descendant of the Oxyd genre, with more than 1000 hand-made levels and a large community of level authors. Its score submission system and monthly Level of the Month keep the community involved.
brief.status: Quiet but alive. The homepage's latest news item is the Enigma 1.30 release on August 27, 2021, and the 1.21 release was December 2014. The homepage footer reads 'Copyright 2003 - 2025', and the GitHub repo is linked as the source. I did not see a commit date, so I cannot say more precisely.
brief.caveats: It is a graphical game that needs a display, so it is not a terminal toy. Linux binaries are not guaranteed; the project itself says packaging for every distro is almost impossible, and building from source is the fallback. The README points to a user manual and tutorials but I did not fetch them. Level sound effects have mixed or unclear origins, and the README asks users to check soundsets/enigma/README before reusing them. The code is GPL v2 or later, with third-party licences in the ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS file. The homepage page content was messy but readable.
quotes: Enigma is a unique puzzle game, with influences from almost every game genre.
Simple? Yes. Easy? It would be, if it weren't for hidden traps, vast mazes, insurmountable obstacles and innumerable puzzles blocking your direct way to the Oxyd stones...
packaging a Linux version that works everywhere is almost impossible, thanks to countless subtle and not-so-subtle differences between each and every Linux distribution.
fetch_log: https://www.nongnu.org/enigma/ - worked. Homepage text includes the description, news items (1.30 released Aug 27 2021; 1.21 Dec 20 2014) and the footer copyright. Navigation labels were visible but most sub-pages were not followed.

https://github.com/Enigma-game/enigma - worked. I guessed this URL from the homepage's 'Source Repository' and 'on GitHub' mentions; it returned the Enigma README (About, Playing, Installation, Compiling, Copying sections).
